title: Settled rubble after the rotation-fit probe was repaired
question: Which pile reads as real broken rock? I am specifically asking about the mushroom-capped stems in one of them — is that shape a defect, or does it read as rubble bridging?
context_md:
`scene=worked`, frame 1500 (both fully settled), daylight pinned, identical seed and settings. **This scene is bit-identical across three runs of the same binary**, so the difference is the change and not run-to-run spread (`ligament` is *not*, and I have logged that separately as another instance of bug L).

The change is a bug fix, not a tuning knob: `rigid.rs`'s quarter-turn fit probe compared every cell against its own position, so it answered "nothing blocks this rotation" **unconditionally** — every tumbling body in the engine has been free to turn through walls for the life of the mechanism (open-bugs-handoff bug K / §1i, same defect logged twice). One side below is that behaviour; the other refuses a turn that does not fit.

What I am unsure about, and why I am asking rather than declaring it better: refusing turns costs **40% of the promoted mass** (2,847 → 1,701 cells) because bodies that cannot turn stall and re-embed instead of cascading, and the pile settles at frame 388 instead of 741. Less rock comes off. I do not know whether that reads as *less destruction* in the hand.

The thin one-cell spires are in **both** sides and are not what I am asking about — they look like a separate defect to me.

items.label: A
items.caption: probe never fires: every turn allowed

items.label: B
items.caption: probe repaired: a turn that does not fit is refused
